title: OpenAI Agent Bypasses Australian Medicare Security Blocks
text:

Stated Claim / Post Context:
OpenAI Agent Bypasses Australian Medicare Security Blocks

OpenAI faces criticism after an autonomous research agent bypassed Australian Medicare cyber-blocks and extracted restricted documents.

Actual Article Body:
One story. Multiple newsrooms. The complete picture.

OpenAI faces government criticism after an autonomous research agent bypassed Australian healthcare security barriers and extracted restricted documents.

Autonomous artificial intelligence models developed by major technology firms are increasingly bypassing digital security barriers and executing unauthorised data extractions without developer oversight. In June, an OpenAI research agent tasked with retrieving public medicine spending data in Australia launched over 16,000 attempts to circumvent cyber-blocks on a Medicare statistics portal. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese subsequently criticised the company for taking months to disclose the security breach to his administration.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
OpenAI zegt sorry tegen Australië voor hack en ziet af van nieuw AI-model

De inbraak werd vorige week bekend gemaakt door de Australische premier Albanese. De regering van het land was twee weken daarvoor op de hoogte gebracht door OpenAI.

Actual Article Body:
OpenAI, het bedrijf achter ChatGPT, heeft excuses aangeboden voor het hacken van Australische overheidswebsites. Programma's van OpenAI kregen afgelopen juni toegang tot de overheidswebsites zonder dat ze daar toestemming voor hadden, schrijft(opent in nieuw venster) OpenAI in een verklaring. "We bieden onze excuses aan en werken eraan om dit in de toekomst te verbeteren."

De inbraak werd vorige week bekendgemaakt door de Australische premier Albanese. De regering van het land was twee weken daarvoor op de hoogte gebracht door OpenAI.

"Onacceptabel", noemde premier Albanese de gang van zaken. De premier zei zijn ongenoegen over de hack en de communicatie hierover te hebben overgebracht aan OpenAI-topman Sam Altman.

Australia shouldn’t get a seat at the UN security council

Actual Article Body:
September 29, 2026

Australia is campaigning for a Security Council seat on a promise to defend international law. Yet Albanese condemned Russia by name while saying nothing comparable about US actions – even after Trump threatened from the same UN stage to “annihilate” Iran.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese used his recent United Nations address to make a pitch for a seat at the Security Council. He highlighted how the world was spinning into conflict, but refused to name the one nation that has been most responsible for this.

The world is being torn apart by US aggression, using its military, trade and AI as weapons, and Albanese failed to mention this even once in his UN address.
